# Startup readback: AI-41

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Harden the existing Windows worker device lifecycle and outbound task protocol, preserving its local-only role. Outcomes: (1) pairing, poll, heartbeat, result submission and revocation remain bound to a registered device and cannot be reused or replayed by another device; (2) claims, leases and revoked-device work follow the existing queue recovery contract; (3) the supported worker version/capabilities and device health are observable while the worker exposes no inbound listener and executes only its bounded signed action catalogue.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-12, AI-13, AI-18 and AI-19 are Done; completion evidence is AI-12 PR #162 (`9238c59b9c43688bf1e3736a4d041d57e5b4af25`), AI-13 PR #167 (`f7782239b2c08d273ea296420e80e5dee5361048`), and AI-19 PR #171 (`daae0525b7a06d897e045390d8d91297d3324276`), with AI-18's queue lease regression also merged. Existing contracts: authenticated-user JWT + fresh AAL2 MFA gate for site registration/revocation; per-device secret and Ed25519 public identity for outbound Edge calls; device-bound queue/lease ownership, audit/correlation and recovery. Using existing `worker-pair`, `worker-poll`, `worker-heartbeat`, `worker-submit-result`, `device-register`, `device-revoke`, shared `worker-auth`, and Windows worker client contracts; integration rules: DB-03, DB-13, ACC-02, OPS-01 and WORKER-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

The confirmed gap was protocol compatibility: the client did not send capability metadata, its advertised version diverged from package metadata, and poll did not reject unsupported workers before queue work. The shared Edge validator now requires the supported minimum version and inventory capability, rejects unknown capabilities before polling, and only offers signed actions when advertised. Heartbeat persists compatibility in the existing heartbeat status so the device UI can show upgrade/block reasons and capabilities. No migration was needed. Private keys remain device-bound, transport outbound HTTPS only, and action execution stays limited to typed signed manifests; no listener, arbitrary remote command execution, or auth/RLS/MFA changes were introduced.

## Hosted proof and readiness

AI-41 explicitly requires live staging sign-off: real Windows worker, fresh MFA via deployed device UI, paired device identity/version/capabilities, Edge poll/heartbeat/result correlation, harmless task completion, cross-device/replay denial, immediate revoke plus safe outstanding-task recovery, fresh re-pair with old credentials still revoked, outbound-only OS/network inspection, and clear block for outdated/incompatible capabilities. A fixed-project, read-only Management API check found 0 active paired staging devices and 0 heartbeats in the last 30 minutes. The existing local scheduled task is the older v0.1.1 and is not running. The staging test will use the v0.2.0 executable in the foreground with separate DPAPI key/secret and state paths under `C:\ProgramData\AI-Operations\staging\`; it will not use or replace the production scheduled task. No live sign-off is claimed. Fresh MFA, staging pairing, and worker execution remain operator-owned and will be requested only after the candidate and artifact are ready.
